findings: The original high-eight-bit mask is nonzero exactly at unsigned value >= 2**56; the HIA nine-byte branch has the same threshold.
After eight continuation bytes the accumulator contains at most 56 bits. The ninth byte contributes all eight bits without masking bit 7; the result fits exactly in u64.
No minimal-length restriction is imposed on decoding: every complete one-to-nine-byte encoding allowed by the original terminator rule yields its accumulated value and consumed length.

Truncated decode exits before write_word. Every encode capacity refusal precedes any output store. The nine-byte write order is 8 then 7 down to 0, matching the original branch. Other writes cover 0 through count-1 and leave the permitted output tail untouched.
